Sworn testimony of David Grusch: 'I was informed in the course of my official duties of a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program to which I was denied access to those additional read-ons when I requested it. I made the decision based on the data I collected to report this information to my superiors and multiple inspectors general and, in effect, becoming a whistleblower. As you know, I have suffered retaliation for my decision'.

Sworn exchange, Rep. Nancy Mace and David Grusch. Mace: 'If you believe we have crashed craft, as stated earlier, do we have the bodies of the pilots who piloted this craft?' Grusch: 'As I have stated publicly already in my News Nation interview, biologics came with some of these recoveries. Yes.' Mace: 'Were they, I guess, human or nonhuman biologics?' Grusch: 'Nonhuman, and that was the assessment of people with direct knowledge on the program I talked to that are currently still on the program.'

Grusch declined on the record to name individuals or facilities in open session - 'I cannot discuss that publicly, but I did provide that information both to the Inspector General and the Intelligence Committees' - and told Rep. Mace that 'The specific documentation I would have to talk to you in a SCIF about.'

desc: On 26 July 2023 at 10:00 am in 2154 Rayburn, the House Committee on Oversight and Accountability's Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs held the first congressional hearing at which a former intelligence officer testified under oath that the United States possesses craft of non-human origin. The witnesses were Ryan Graves, formerly of VFA-11 and now executive director of Americans for Safe Aerospace; retired Cdr. David Fravor, former commanding officer of VFA-41 and the lead aircrew on the 14 November 2004 Nimitz intercept; and David Grusch, former National Reconnaissance Office representative to the Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Task Force. Rep. Tim Burchett and Rep. Anna Paulina Luna drove the hearing; James Comer chaired the full committee. Three things came out of it that the board treats as permanent. Fravor placed on the record, in writing and under oath, that after the most corroborated encounter in the modern record 'the incident was never investigated, none of my crew were ever questioned, tapes were never taken.' Grusch testified that he had been informed of a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse-engineering programme, that he had provided the information to the Intelligence Community Inspector General and to Congress, that he knew the exact locations and had provided them to the ICIG and the Intelligence committees in classified session, and that he had witnessed and reported administrative terrorism against colleagues. Graves testified to the operational reporting problem in the Atlantic operating areas. What did not come out of it is equally important: no contractor was called, no document production was compelled, and the 'specific cooperative and hostile witness list' Grusch offered Rep. Nancy Mace under oath has never been produced publicly. The hearing established the subject as legitimate congressional business and simultaneously demonstrated the limits of a committee without jurisdiction over the compartments it is asking about.

claims.text: The subcommittee met at 10:06 a.m. on 26 July 2023 in room 2154, Rayburn House Office Building, Rep. Glenn Grothman presiding; present were Grothman, Gosar, Foxx, Sessions, Biggs, Mace, LaTurner, Armstrong, Perry, Garcia, Moskowitz and Frost, with Luna, Burlison, Gaetz, Burchett, Comer, Ogles, Langworthy, Raskin and Ocasio-Cortez also present.

Rep. Burchett stated on the record that members 'were even denied access to a classified briefing in a SCIF prior to this hearing due to the amount of hoops that we had to jump through to grant temporary clearance to witness Grusch, who has knowledge of classified information.'

Grusch's written opening statement states: 'I was informed, in the course of my official duties, of a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program to which I was denied access to those additional read-on's.'

Grusch's written statement records that he became a whistleblower 'through a PPD-19 Urgent Concern filing with the Intelligence Community Inspector General (ICIG)', and that 'In 2019, the UAPTF director tasked me to identify all Special Access Programs & Controlled Access Programs (SAPs/CAPs) we needed to satisfy our congressionally mandated mission.'

Asked by Rep. Moskowitz how such a programme is funded, Grusch answered: 'I will give you generalities. I can get very specific in a closed session. But misappropriation of funds and self-fund.' Asked whether budgeted money is diverted, he said: 'Yes. I have specific knowledge of that. Yes.'

Asked by Rep. Ocasio-Cortez about defence contractor involvement, Grusch described 'the contractors, you know, or the metal benders, so to speak, the ones actually doing specific performance on government contracts'; asked whether contractors must report UAP sightings, he answered: 'In terms of the contractors? Not that I am aware of.'

Asked by Rep. Burchett to name people with firsthand knowledge of crash retrieval programmes, Grusch said: 'I cannot discuss that publicly, but I did provide that information both to the intel committees and the Inspector General.'

Asked when the US Government first became aware of non-human intelligence, Grusch answered: 'I like to use the term nonhuman. I do not like to denote origin. Keeps the aperture open both scientifically. Certainly, like I have discussed publicly, previously 1930's.'

Asked by Rep. Burlison whether he had seen the bodies, Grusch answered: 'That is something I have not witnessed myself.' On the craft he said: 'I have to be careful to describe what I have seen firsthand and not in this environment.'

Fravor's written statement to the committee states: 'What is shocking is that the incident was never investigated, none of my crew were ever questioned, tapes were never taken, and after a couple of days, it turned into a great story to tell friends.'

Fravor's written statement frames the issue as an oversight failure: 'even Unacknowledged Waived programs have some level of oversight by the appropriate committee members in the House and Senate and this work that is said to be occurring from Whistleblower testimonies should not be exempt.'

A member read AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick's prior congressional testimony into the record as the counter-position: that there has been 'no credible evidence thus far of extraterrestrial activity' or of 'off-world technology brought to the attention of the office'.

The Committee's own hearing wrap-up release lists its Key Takeaways as poor federal reporting processes and retaliation against pilots, and quotes Graves estimating that pilots report 'somewhere near five percent' of sightings; crash retrieval, non-human craft and contractor custody appear nowhere in the committee's published summary.

No defence contractor representative was called as a witness and no document production was compelled at this hearing, despite contractor custody being raised on the record by two members and the witness.

dossier.denialPosture: The Department of Defense's position at the hearing was represented only indirectly, through a member quoting AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick's prior testimony that there is 'no credible evidence thus far of extraterrestrial activity' and no 'off-world technology brought to the attention of the office'. No DoD or AARO witness appeared, and the Department made no on-the-record response to the funding-diversion or contractor-custody testimony.
dossier.narrative:
The subcommittee met at 10:06 a.m. on 26 July 2023 in 2154 Rayburn. Present were Representatives Grothman, Gosar, Foxx, Sessions, Biggs, Mace, LaTurner, Armstrong, Perry, Garcia, Moskowitz and Frost; also present, waived on, were Luna, Burlison, Gaetz, Burchett, Comer, Ogles, Langworthy, Raskin and Ocasio-Cortez. The unusual size of the 'also present' list is the first fact about this hearing: members from outside the subcommittee, from both parties, came to sit in.

The second fact came in Burchett's opening. Members, he said, 'were even denied access to a classified briefing in a SCIF prior to this hearing due to the amount of hoops that we had to jump through to grant temporary clearance to witness Grusch, who has knowledge of classified information.' The committee therefore held a public hearing about compartmented programmes without the means to hear about compartmented programmes. Every subsequent deferral in the transcript traces back to that.

Grusch's written opening statement is the core document. He identifies himself as an intelligence officer of fourteen years, a USAF major, and from 2021 to 2023 a GS-15 at the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, where he was his agency's co-lead for UAP and transmedium object analysis reporting to the UAP Task Force and then to AARO. He states that he became a whistleblower 'through a PPD-19 Urgent Concern filing with the Intelligence Community Inspector General (ICIG)'. He describes a specific tasking: 'In 2019, the UAPTF director tasked me to identify all Special Access Programs & Controlled Access Programs (SAPs/CAPs) we needed to satisfy our congressionally mandated mission.' And then the sentence the hearing is remembered for: 'I was informed, in the course of my official duties, of a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program to which I was denied access to those additional read-on's.' His closing statement calls the programmes he reported the 'Non-Human Reverse Engineering Programs' and predicts their revelation would act as 'an ontological (earth-shattering) shock'.

Under questioning the mechanism claims sharpened. Asked by Rep. Moskowitz how such a programme gets funded, Grusch answered: 'I will give you generalities. I can get very specific in a closed session. But misappropriation of funds and self-fund.' Asked whether that meant money budgeted for one programme goes elsewhere, he said 'Yes. I have specific knowledge of that. Yes.' Asked by Rep. Ocasio-Cortez about interactions between defence contractors and UAP activities, he described 'the contractors, you know, or the metal benders, so to speak, the ones actually doing specific performance on government contracts.' Asked whether those contractors are required to report UAP sightings, he answered: 'In terms of the contractors? Not that I am aware of.' That single exchange is the cleanest statement on the record of the regulatory gap that would allow contractor custody to persist without disclosure.

On where and who, he refused in open session and said the information had gone elsewhere: 'I cannot discuss that publicly, but I did provide that information both to the intel committees and the Inspector General.' Asked by Burchett whether it could be given in a SCIF, he replied 'Sure, if you had the appropriate accesses.' Asked when the government first became aware, he said: 'I like to use the term nonhuman. I do not like to denote origin. Keeps the aperture open both scientifically. Certainly, like I have discussed publicly, previously 1930's.' Asked by Rep. Burlison whether he had personally seen the craft or bodies, he distinguished carefully: on the craft, 'I have to be careful to describe what I have seen firsthand and not in this environment'; on bodies, 'That is something I have not witnessed myself.' The witness is testifying to what he was told and what he documented, not to personal observation, and the transcript is unambiguous that he drew that line himself.

Fravor's written statement supplies the other half. He commanded VFA-41 aboard USS Nimitz in November 2004 and describes the Princeton having tracked the objects on Aegis 'for the previous 2 weeks', descending from above 80,000 feet to 20,000 feet, staying for hours, and going 'straight back up'. His closing judgement is about oversight, not phenomenology: 'even Unacknowledged Waived programs have some level of oversight by the appropriate committee members in the House and Senate and this work that is said to be occurring from Whistleblower testimonies should not be exempt.' And the line that indicts the system: 'What is shocking is that the incident was never investigated, none of my crew were ever questioned, tapes were never taken, and after a couple of days, it turned into a great story to tell friends.'

The official denial was read into the record by a member reciting AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick's prior testimony that there has been 'no credible evidence thus far of extraterrestrial activity' or of 'off-world technology brought to the attention of the office' - a formulation that is a statement about what reached one office, not about what exists.

What the hearing did not produce is as important as what it did. No contractor was called. No document was subpoenaed. The Committee's own wrap-up release, published the same day, lists its Key Takeaways as poor reporting processes and retaliation against pilots, and quotes Graves estimating that only 'somewhere near five percent' of pilot sightings are reported. Crash retrieval, non-human craft and contractor custody do not appear in the committee's summary of its own hearing.
openQuestions: Grusch stated he provided names, locations and documentation to the ICIG and the intelligence committees; none of that material has been published or acknowledged as received in any public committee document.
Whether the classified session Grusch repeatedly offered was ever held on the terms he described, and by which committee.
Which Special Access Programs Grusch identified in his 2019 UAPTF tasking, and whether that tasking product still exists as a retrievable document.

The publicly retrievable copies of the printed record (CHRG-118hhrg53022) and the committee transcript PDF both truncate before the closing rounds of questioning; a complete verified text of the final third of the hearing has not been obtained for this dossier.
No contractor named in open or closed session has been publicly identified, and no committee has issued a subpoena arising from this hearing.
dossier.whatItIs: A hearing of the House Committee on Oversight and Accountability's Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs, held 26 July 2023 at 10:06 a.m. in room 2154 of the Rayburn House Office Building, chaired by Rep. Glenn Grothman. The witnesses were Ryan Graves, David Grusch and retired Commander David Fravor. It was the first congressional hearing at which a former intelligence officer testified under oath that the United States operates a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse-engineering programme outside congressional oversight.
dossier.whyImplicated: This hearing converted the legacy programme allegation from journalism into sworn testimony before a committee of jurisdiction, and it did so with three specific mechanisms attached: how the programme is hidden (special access programs the witness was denied read-on to), how it is paid for (misappropriation of funds and self-funding), and who holds the material (contractors, described by the witness as 'the metal benders', who are under no requirement to report UAP). Fravor's written statement establishes that the most corroborated modern military encounter was never investigated and the tapes were never collected - an evidentiary vacuum that is itself the artefact. The hearing also demonstrated the ceiling on congressional capability: members were denied a SCIF, no contractor was called, no document production was compelled, and every substantive answer was deferred to a closed session that has never been publicly confirmed to have occurred on these terms. The committee's own wrap-up release then framed the day around pilot reporting and stigma, omitting the crash retrieval testimony entirely.

entityInfo.desc: Key exchanges from the official transcript, verbatim where quoted. Grothman to Grusch on what was hidden: 'Both material acquisition and exploitation activity, also baselining the UAPs but not sharing it with intelligence professionals that are actually doing step briefs to pilots.' Garcia: 'do you believe that our government is in possession of UAPs?' Grusch: 'Absolutely, based on interviewing over 40 witnesses over 4 years.' Garcia: 'And where?' Grusch: 'I know the exact locations and those locations were provided to the Inspector General and some of which to the intelligence committees. I actually had the people with the firsthand knowledge provide a protected disclosure to the Inspector General.' Burchett on harm: 'Do you have any personal knowledge of people who have been harmed or injured in efforts to cover up or conceal these extraterrestrial technology?' Grusch: 'Yes, personally.' Burchett on murder: Grusch: 'I have to be careful answering that question. I directed people with that knowledge to the appropriate authorities.' Burchett then noted the members had been denied access to a SCIF. Mace: 'If you believe we have crashed craft, as stated earlier, do we have the bodies of the pilots who piloted this craft?' Grusch: 'As I have stated publicly already in my News Nation interview, biologics came with some of these recoveries. Yes.' Mace: 'Were they, I guess, human or nonhuman biologics?' Grusch: 'Nonhuman, and that was the assessment of people with direct knowledge on the program I talked to that are currently still on the program.' Mace on who to call next: Grusch: 'I can give you a specific cooperative and hostile witness list of specific individuals that were in those.' Moskowitz on funding: Grusch: 'misappropriation of funds and self-fund'; on contractor overcharging: 'Correct, through something called IR&D'; on notification: 'IR&D is literally internal to the contractors. So, as long as it is money, either profits, private investment, et cetera, they do whatever they want.' Moskowitz on statute: Grusch cited 10 U.S.C. 119, the Deputy Secretary's ability to waive congressional reporting, and the Gang of Eight notification requirement for a waived unacknowledged SAP. Foxx on Kirkpatrick's prior testimony that AARO had seen no credible evidence: Grusch: 'It is not accurate,' adding that a few of the roughly 30 individuals who had come to AARO were people he had also interviewed and whose material he had evaluated. Luna on the AARO director: 'Him and I had a classified conversation in April 2022 before he took over AARO in July 2022 and I provided him some concerns I had.' Luna on clearance to speak: 'Correct, through DODSR - DoD Prepublication and Security Review.' Ocasio-Cortez on contractors: whether they must report UAP activity - 'In terms of the contractors? Not that I am aware of.' Burchett on injuries in the legacy program: 'Yes,' with Grusch declining specifics but noting the hazards of assessing an unknown unknown.

timeline.label: Hearing noticed
timeline.text: The Oversight National Security subcommittee announces a UAP hearing with Graves, Grusch and Fravor as witnesses.

timeline.label: Aviators testify to House Oversight
timeline.text: Fravor and Graves testify alongside David Grusch. Fravor's statement: 'the incident was never investigated, none of my crew were ever questioned, tapes were never taken.'

timeline.label: The founding hearing
timeline.text: Grothman gavels in the first modern House UAP hearing in 2154 Rayburn and waives Burchett, Luna, Gaetz, Burlison, Ocasio-Cortez and Ogles onto the subcommittee.

timeline.label: Sworn testimony before House Oversight
timeline.text: Grusch testifies to a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse engineering program, over 40 witnesses interviewed across four years, nonhuman biologics recovered with craft, personal knowledge of people harmed, and funding by misappropriation and contractor IR&D. Members state they were denied a SCIF.

timeline.label: House Oversight UAP hearing
timeline.text: George Knapp attends; the hearing establishes the congressional venue that Shellenberger will use sixteen months later.

timeline.label: Grusch names IR&D under oath
timeline.text: Asked how unreported programs are funded, Grusch answers 'misappropriation of funds and self-fund,' then identifies IR&D as the channel, and tells the committee that contractors have no obligation to report UAP encounters.

timeline.label: Grusch testifies to House Oversight under oath
timeline.text: The House Oversight Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs hears Ryan Graves, David Grusch and Cdr. David Fravor (Ret.) in room 2154 Rayburn. Grusch testifies that he 'was informed in the course of my official duties of a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program to which I was denied access', and, asked whether recovered biologics were human or nonhuman, answers 'Nonhuman'. Printed as Serial No. 118-53 (CHRG-118hhrg53022).

timeline.label: Grusch, Fravor and Graves testify
timeline.text: The first congressional hearing at which a former intelligence officer testifies under oath to a multi-decade crash retrieval programme. No contractor is called and no document production is compelled.
